title: Cap. III Rej. Rat. 1: reprobates only under 'if they will' — not equal termini
pass_a_gloss: As for those to be reprobated, he did not have a will that referred proximately to their salvation: for those who defend that are forced to add this rider, If they themselves have willed. Since therefore God foresees this their Not-willing, and does not will to give them that which he really gives to the elect, it is manifest that this will of God is not terminated equally to the salvation of the elect and of the non-elect.
pass_b_english: Toward the reprobate he had no will aimed next at their salvation: defenders must tack on "if they themselves will." Since God foresees their Not-willing and will not give them what he really gives the elect, that will clearly does not terminate equally on elect and non-elect salvation.
source_text: Quoad reprobandos, non habuit voluntatem quae proxime referebatur ad eorum salutem: nam qui id defendunt, coguntur hoc additamentum apponere, Si ipsi voluerint. Cum ergo Deus praevideat hoc ipsorum Nolle, & nolit illis dare id, quod revera dat electis, manifestum est hanc voluntatem Dei non ex aequo terminari ad salutem electorum & non-electorum.
